NeerTrack Case Study
◈ UX Case Study · Jorhat, Assam · 2025

When water
runs on silence.

NeerTrack is a civic digital product designed to bridge the communication gap between Jorhat residents and their water utility — turning anxiety into awareness.

"We only knew when it was too late — the water was already gone."

— Survey respondent · Jorhat, Assam · 2025

Phase 01 — Discover

The problem wasn't water.
It was the silence around it.

In Jorhat — a Tier 4 city in Assam — the local water utility communicates through phone calls and outdated website notices. Residents wake up not knowing if water will come, how long it will last, or what quality it will be.

⏰
Water Outages Without Warning
Supply disappears without advance notice. Residents discover the outage only when they turn the tap.
💸
Paying More for Less
"Even with low quality service we have to pay higher amounts." Residents report above-normal charges.
⚙️
Faulty Infrastructure, No Updates
Broken filter machines and aging pipes cause quality degradation with no status communication.
📵
No Reporting Channel
Residents who want to report leaks have no clear digital channel. Phone calls go unanswered.
💪
High-Wattage Motor Inequity
Wealthier households use large motors, leaving lower-income areas without adequate supply.
🌊
Deteriorating Source Quality
The river source is degrading over time, with residents having no visibility into quality data.
Phase 01 — Research Methods

What the residents actually said — and what they didn't.

A small online survey (fewer than 20 responses) of Jorhat residents aged 30–70: working professionals, homemakers and wage workers. Findings are directional, not statistically representative.

📋 Survey Goals

  • What is causing the water supply problem in Jorhat specifically?
  • Main pain points and daily frustrations of residents
  • Whether the problem is systemic or zone-specific
  • How the utility currently manages complaints

💡 Key Insights Surfaced

"We missed this time also." — on irregular water windows
"We only knew when it's too late."
  • Monitoring system + alert feature ranked highest in resident wish lists
  • Motor inequity is a socioeconomic equity issue, not just technical
Phase 01 — Synthesis

Affinity mapping: four clusters, four design solutions.

Raw survey responses were grouped into behavioural clusters. Each cluster directly maps to a design intervention.

Cluster 01
No timely distribution
"We missed this time also."
→ Alert feature
Cluster 02
High charges, low quality
"Even with low quality we pay higher amounts."
→ Monitoring + analytics
Cluster 03
Faulty filter machines
"Authority is unable to repair the machines."
→ Status notifications
Cluster 04
Motor inequity problem
"Higher wattage motors consume most of the water."
→ Report feature

Inside the mind of a Jorhat resident on a water outage morning.

Synthesised from open-ended survey responses and lived experience patterns across participant types.

Think / Feel

  • Even if water is there, quality is poor.
  • What if there's no water tomorrow?
See

  • Empty buckets waiting at 6am
  • WhatsApp groups flooded with "no water"
Hear

  • "Supply period was short again."
  • "Poor quality, don't use it."

Phase 02 — Define

Point of view statements → How might we questions.

Each persona translated into a POV, then into a design-actionable HMW question — the north stars guiding every feature decision.

Rupam Das · Wage Worker

Rupam struggles to get to work on time because unpredictable water supply forces him to wait without knowing how long.

How might we alert Rupam in advance about distribution time so he can plan his commute?
Sweta Gogoi · Homemaker

Sweta is unable to complete household chores because she cannot predict when water will arrive.

How might we help Sweta know in advance about outages so she can prepare storage?
Rituraj Bora · Businessman

Rituraj cannot trust the water quality, leading to significant extra household expense on bottled water.

How might we help Rituraj's family know clearly whether today's water is safe?
Bitupan Ghosh · Student

Bitupan gets late to college because he has no way to check water status before his morning routine.

How might we give Bitupan a reliable, at-a-glance morning water status check?
Core UX Problem

Jorhat residents lack a reliable, real-time communication channel with their water utility — creating daily anxiety, financial waste, and a feeling of complete helplessness.

The goal: design a digital solution that gives residents proactive supply information, a trusted reporting channel, and enough transparency to feel in control — even when the water doesn't come.

Phase 04 — Deliver

Six design decisions that shaped the final product.

Each decision driven by research and tested against one constraint: usable equally by a 50-year-old homemaker and a 24-year-old student.

01
Status-first home screen
The single most important morning question is "is there water?" — the home screen answers this first.
02
OTP-based login
Consumer number + OTP avoids password fatigue for a largely non-technical user base while keeping accounts secure.
03
Photo is optional
Users in a hurry can file a complaint in under 60 seconds without needing a camera.
04
Ticket ID + status tracking
Directly addresses the complaint black hole — residents now see a clear reference ID and can check status anytime.
05
Quality readings + plain-language tooltip
Technical readings (pH, turbidity, chlorine, hardness) shown directly, with a tap-to-learn tooltip explaining what's normal.
06
Multi-language settings
English, Assamese, Bengali, and Hindi toggle — accommodating Jorhat's actual linguistic makeup.
Phase 04 — Impact

Before NeerTrack. After NeerTrack, by design.

A comparison of design intent, not of measured results. NeerTrack has not been deployed or tested with residents yet.

Before — Current state (as described by survey respondents)
  • Outages discovered by turning on a dry tap at 6am
  • No advance supply schedule visible
  • Water quality unknown to residents
  • Complaints via phone — unanswered, no ticket
  • Limited language support reported
After — NeerTrack (design intent, untested)
  • Designed to push an alert ahead of a scheduled outage
  • Weekly supply schedule on home screen
  • Water quality readings with a plain-language tooltip
  • 3-step flow with Ticket ID + status tracking
  • Assamese / Hindi / Bengali / English toggle

Phase 04 — Hypotheses

Hypothesis matrix: what I expect, and how I'll prove it.

None of these are measured results. Targets come from benchmarks of comparable civic apps (NextDrop India, BWSSB Bangalore, NYC 311) and stay unvalidated until the planned usability test and a one-ward pilot.

IDHypothesisMetricBaseline todayTargetBenchmark basisHow I'll validateStatus

Read it left to right: assumption → how it is measured → where it starts → where I think it can go → how it gets proven. If a test disproves a hypothesis, the feature is redesigned, not defended.

Validation

Usability testing: what's planned and why it matters.

Formal usability testing was not conducted within this 14-day sprint — this is a documented plan for the next step.

🔬

Planned Usability Test Protocol

A moderated usability test with 5 Jorhat residents — one from each persona type plus one cross-type. Sessions run 20 minutes via Google Meet or in-person.

Three core tasks:

  1. Find today's water supply status and explain what it means
  2. File a complaint about a leaking pipe near your home
  3. Check what time water will come on Thursday this week

Success metrics: Task completion 80%+, complaint filing under 90 seconds, SUS score 75+.

Retrospective

What I'd do differently. What surprised me.

The honest retrospective.

What worked well

Anchoring every feature to a specific persona's pain point kept scope from exploding. Every feature held back from the MVP had a documented reason.

What I'd change

I'd run informal walkthrough tests at wireframe stage, not just at high-fidelity — flow ambiguities would surface far earlier.

What surprised me

The motor inequity finding turned a technical supply problem into a social justice issue — it reshaped how I framed the reporting feature entirely.

NeerTrack · Water Supply Management App · Jorhat, Assam · UI/UX Case Study · 2025
